# Navimower Map Card 0.3.7-beta15

## Prepared History frontend

This prerelease moves completed History rendering onto the Prepared History
backend introduced by Navimower 0.4.5-beta26.

The visual History contract is intentionally unchanged: completed sessions still
render the same backend-generated mowed-area and travel SVG paths. What changes
is discovery, transport and caching.

### Single mower

When beta26 advertises `history_ready_manifest`, the card now prefers the
authenticated ready-only History manifest instead of the older Sessions index.

The manifest supplies:

- retained completed-session metadata;
- per-session `render_ready` state;
- immutable `resource_id`;
- content-addressed resource URL;
- legacy session-render fallback URL.

For a ready completed session the card fetches
`/api/navimower/history-resource/.../{resource_id}` and renders the returned
SVG-ready artifact directly.

The old `/session-render/.../{session_id}` endpoint is used only when:

- Prepared History is not advertised;
- the manifest is incompatible/unavailable;
- a session is not ready yet;
- the prepared resource request fails.

### Shared content-addressed browser cache

Prepared History resources are cached by `resource_id`, not session id or card
instance.

The cache is module-wide and shared by:

- repeated History opens;
- multiple Navimower Map Card instances;
- Single and Multi mower views.

If Single view has already loaded a completed-session resource, switching to
Multi view can reuse that exact render without downloading it again.

Concurrent requests for the same immutable resource are also coalesced behind a
shared in-flight promise.

### Multi mower

Member metadata now prefers each member's beta26 History manifest when exposed
through Site/frontend metadata.

Member completed-session rendering uses the same shared Prepared History resource
loader/cache as Single view. Existing per-member site transforms are still
applied at render time, so resources remain mower-local while presentation
remains site-wide.

Legacy member Sessions/session-render paths remain complete fallbacks.

### Prewarm handling

If a beta26 manifest is still prewarming and reports pending retained sessions,
the Single runtime schedules a short manifest retry. A session without a ready
descriptor can still use the existing legacy session-render fallback, so History
does not become unusable during startup.

## Compatibility

Recommended pair:

- Navimower 0.4.5-beta26+
- Navimower Map Card 0.3.7-beta15

Older integrations remain supported through the existing History fallback.

No live-route, current-cycle, mower position, Schedule, commands, map geometry
or underlay behavior changes in this beta.

## Legacy removal policy

Beta15 intentionally does **not** delete the old frontend History/session-render
code yet.

After field testing confirms that beta26 reports all retained eligible sessions
ready and beta15 consumes the new resources correctly, the next cleanup can
remove redundant frontend raw/daily-trail/legacy History paths. Backend
compatibility endpoints should only be removed after that cleanup is proven.

## Regression coverage

The beta15 regression verifies:

- beta26 ready-only History manifest adoption;
- prepared descriptor retention on normalized session metadata;
- immutable resource fetch by `resource_id`;
- no legacy session-render request when a prepared resource is ready;
- shared manifest/resource reuse across separate card instances;
- older-integration Sessions/session-render fallback;
- Multi runtime wiring to the same Prepared History loader.

The cumulative runtime does not gain a new wrapper or IIFE.

## Recommended field test

After installing Navimower 0.4.5-beta26, first confirm:

- `prepared_history.prewarm_complete: true`;
- `ready_session_count == eligible_session_count`;
- `pending_session_count: 0`;
- zero Prepared History build/index failures.

Then install Map Card beta15 and open completed History in Single and Multi
views.

Expected beta26 diagnostics after viewing History:

- `prepared_history.manifest_reads > 0`;
- `prepared_history.resource_reads > 0`;
- `prepared_history.resource_bytes_served_total > 0`;
- `prepared_history.legacy_render_reads` should stay at zero when every viewed
  session is ready;
- reopening the same sessions or switching Single -> Multi should reuse the
  frontend resource cache and avoid proportional resource-read growth.
